title: What is a TLAB and how does it make allocation fast?
shortTitle: What is a TLAB and how does it make allocation fast?
keyPoints: TLAB = Thread-Local Allocation Buffer: a private region of Eden space per thread
Allocation is just bumping a pointer – no locking, no contention
When the TLAB fills up, the thread gets a new one from Eden
TLABs make new Object() nearly as cheap as a stack allocation
Default size: dynamically tuned by the JVM based on thread allocation rate

s1_definition.oneliner: TLAB is a per-thread private buffer in Eden space. Object allocation is a lock-free pointer bump, making new extremely fast.
s1_definition.profdef:
TLAB mechanics:

- Each thread gets a private chunk of Eden space.
- Allocating an object = increment a pointer. No lock needed.
- When the TLAB fills, the thread requests a new one from Eden.
- This eliminates allocation contention in multi-threaded apps.
s1_definition.analogy: Each bank teller has their own supply of blank forms (TLAB). They do not need to go to the central supply room (shared heap) for every form. When their stack runs out, they get a new batch. No waiting, no contention.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Without TLAB:  every new Object() → lock → allocate → unlock → contention
  With TLAB:     every new Object() → bump thread-local pointer → no lock

  TLAB lifecycle:
    Thread starts → gets TLAB from Eden
    Allocate → pointer bump (fast)
    TLAB full → get new TLAB → old one stays in Eden for GC
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
TLAB is a per-thread private buffer in Eden. Allocation is a lock-free pointer bump, making new Object() nearly as fast as a stack allocation. This is why Java object creation is cheap despite being heap-allocated.

One sentence to remember: TLAB gives each thread its own allocation buffer – new is just a pointer bump with no lock.
